scope: targeted (30 at-risk rows: 13 axis_orphans + 17 thin_no_instrument). 56 likely_carry accepted as carry.
method: re-sourced ambiguous/blank-candidate rows via WebSearch (local officials); instrument-evidenced moves/carries judged from existing sources. Dispositions apply to the SEASON 2 answer set at assembly; Season 1 untouched.

rows.justification: City Attorney candidate; sanitation lever is prosecution. Platform reopens the Environmental Crimes Unit to target polluters — matches chair-3 'target enforcement at the businesses and large property owners who create the most waste'. No service-expansion instrument (chair 1).

Re-source found a concrete provision instrument: proposes non-punitive 'spot cleaning' (routine trash collection + waste disposal at encampments) plus clearing a 50,000 sidewalk-repair backlog district-wide. Expand/provide services = chair 1.

Re-source found only committee seats (Health & Human Needs) and a homelessness services-over-enforcement stance. No city-sanitation instrument on any chair. Blank per 're-source first, blank if none'.

100% organic-waste diversion, zero-waste + producer-accountability, strengthen the Bureau of Sanitation's capacity = significantly expand public sanitation services (chair 1). No worst-served concentration policy (chair 2).

Supported FY-budget funding for the new Clean City Team (rapid-response dumping/graffiti) = expansion (chair 1). West-side dumping work is constituent response, not a stated citywide worst-served-concentration policy. Borderline 1/2.
As Council Chair led the FY26 budget that CREATED a new Clean City Team for waste removal/illegal dumping/graffiti on city property = expand public sanitation services (chair 1).

Record is defend-existing-funding ('enough cuts') + sponsored unwinding Prop B's separate Sanitation Dept, and opposes enforcement-led responses. That is maintain-services BUT explicitly anti-enforcement, so it contradicts chair-3's enforcement clause and is not expansion (1) or worst-served concentration (2). No clean v2 chair fits.
Re-source: seeks to expand Public Works' street-cleaning budget for the Mission with 'sustainable, permanent funding' = expand public sanitation services (chair 1). Rescued from blank.
Proposes rapid-response cleanup teams and increased trash collection near schools/parks/transit/commercial corridors = expand public sanitation services (chair 1).
Proposes city-emptied designated dump zones and rapid-response teams = new/expanded city provision (chair 1).
Quality of Life Team, year-round Keep Worcester Clean multi-department coordination, and a Zero Waste Master Plan = significantly expand public sanitation services (chair 1).

Record is efficient delivery of existing basic services (audits, briefing requests) and opposing the regressive trash-bag fee = maintain current services (chair 3). Enforcement-at-business clause not evidenced (flag). Not expansion (1) or worst-served concentration (2).
Co-sponsored the snow-corps exploration order to have the city take over public-sidewalk clearing ('the current system isn't working') = expand city sanitation responsibility (chair 1).
Spearheaded a city-wide glass-recycling program and supports expanding recycling infrastructure = expand public sanitation services (chair 1).

Funded the Downtown Streets Team expansion to Gilman for twice-weekly cleaning and frames poor conditions as a services failure requiring active city response = expand public sanitation services (chair 1).

Only sanitation evidence is a single quote of enthusiasm for someone else's snow-corps proposal; re-source found no sanitation platform. A soft endorsement is not an instrument that seats a chair. Blank.

Platform directs sanitation resources into underinvested communities and prioritizes reducing illegal dumping in North Sacramento / Del Paso Heights = concentrate resources on the most neglected neighborhoods (chair 2). Equity direction matches v2.
2025 questionnaire targets clean streets and needle cleanup for the high-need Mass & Cass area with city resources = concentrate on the worst-served (chair 2). Equity direction matches v2.

Concrete sanitation instrument is a Board motion on untreated-sewage spills (regional environmental oversight, off the neighborhood-cleanliness axis); the underserved-South-LA beautification language is not a worst-served sanitation-resource-concentration instrument. No clean v2 chair fits.

Signature position is eliminating/pausing the trash fee (free access) framed as services residents 'rightfully deserve' = expand public sanitation access as a city responsibility (chair 1). Universal services-first, not worst-served concentration.

Stated goal is equitable resource distribution to districts 'historically isolated and disenfranchised', service investment in historically neglected areas = concentrate on the worst-served (chair 2). Equity direction matches v2.
Negotiated a hauler contract adding affordable mid-tier bulk pickup = maintain/improve access to current services (chair 3).
Public Works Committee member; constituent street-resurfacing petitions, no expansion/privatization = maintain current services (chair 3).
Environment-committee chair overseeing the Green Worcester Plan and environmental-standards enforcement rather than service expansion = maintain + enforce (chair 3).
'Safe and Clean' theme, clean public spaces as a maintain-and-keep-orderly priority = maintain current services (chair 3).
Maintain/improve current services with anti-dumping enforcement as the primary tool = chair 3 (maintain + enforcement).
Backed the Incident Management Team removing encampment trash while enforcing anti-dumping/encampment laws = maintain + enforce (chair 3).
Negotiated reduced trash fees, maintains services and opposes fee increases while enforcing anti-dumping for businesses = chair 3 (maintain + business enforcement).
Standard municipal DPW model, no expansion or privatization stance = maintain current services (chair 3).
Constituency-driven maintenance plus 41.18 debris-removal enforcement, no expansion legislation = maintain + enforce (chair 3).
